name: Scroll reveal
summary: Sections and cards that fade and rise into place as they scroll into view, plus page transitions.
description:
Use reveals sparingly on marketing pages, on section content and groups of cards, to give a page some life as it is read. Never on app screens people use all day.

They are pure CSS on view timelines: .v-reveal rises, -left and -right come from the start or end side, -scale grows, and .v-reveal-stagger reveals its children one after another. They only run when the reader has no reduced-motion preference and the browser has view timelines; everywhere else the content simply shows.

Page transitions are a separate opt-in file, dist/vectra.transitions.css: load it and same-site page loads cross-fade (cross-document view transitions, no JS). Give an element on two pages the same view-transition-name and it morphs between them.

classes.name: v-reveal
classes.description: Rises and fades in as it enters the viewport.

classes.name: v-reveal-left
classes.description: With .v-reveal: comes in from the start side (mirrored in right to left).

classes.name: v-reveal-right
classes.description: With .v-reveal: comes in from the end side.

classes.name: v-reveal-stagger
classes.description: On a grid or list: each child reveals a little after the one before (up to five steps).

a11y: Off under prefers-reduced-motion, and nothing is ever hidden: without view timelines the content shows straight away.
Reveals run on scroll position, not on a timer, so content is never invisible while the reader looks at it.
Page transitions are off under reduced motion too.

examples.title: Staggered cards and a side reveal
examples.description: Scroll the preview; with reduced motion on, they simply show.
